newsitem.title: FRANCE: Albanian writer Kadare warns of genocide risk.
newsitem.headline: Albanian writer Kadare warns of genocide risk.

text.p: Albanian writer Ismail Kadare said on Monday his homeland risked a genocide if the international community did not intervene.
"Albania has never been so close to suicide," Kadare, author of "The Concert" and "The General of the Dead Army", told Reuters.

He said "energetic international arbitration" was essential, including the sending of a peacekeeping force acting as a military barrier. "If not, there is a risk of genocide," he said, adding "Balkan countries listen to international arbitrations".
He hailed an agreement reached on Sunday between Albanian leaders and the opposition as "a first serious step by a political class which until now has shown itself incapable of resolving the crisis."
Kadare, who now lives in both Paris and Tirana, sought political asylum in France in October 1990 before the Albanian Communist government fell. He said complete irrationality ruled in the southwest.

Anti-government forces seized control of most of southern Albania on Monday, leaving the army in disarray and dismissing the deal forged by President Sali Berisha and the opposition for a political end to the conflict.
